newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - ING Q1 net seen up 20 pct-plus.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - ING Q1 net seen up 20 pct-plus.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV's strong profit momentum is forecast to have continued into the new year, driving earnings up more than 20 percent in the first quarter of 1997, analysts said.
They forecast net profit before preference dividends at between 850 million and 946 million guilders, with a consensus estimate of 894 milion, up 21 percent on a year earlier.
Such an outcome would be consistent with executive board chairman Aad Jacobs' statement at the annual meeting earlier this month that first quarter results would look excellent.
First quarter results will be published on Thursday.
Analysts said that as with the 1996 results, growth in profits from banking would outstrip that of insurance but insurance would remain the bigger profit contributor.
"Trading results should be very good in the securities division. You have seen that from all (banks') securities operations around the world," said Tom Bennett, an analyst with Paribas in London.

ING's 25.4 percent leap in full year 1996 earnings was driven by a 33.7 percent increase in commissions and a 25.9 percent advance in financial transactions income, due partly to excellent share market conditions.
Bennett noted that growth in ING's loan portfolio accelerated through 1996, rising 21.2 percent over the year.
Kempen and Co analyst Hans Pluijgers said the continued growth in bank lending in the first three months of the year would have contributed to a strong rise in interest income.
Pluijgers forecast continued double-digit growth in premium income from the insurance operations as well as good profits from life and non-life operations.
He predicted a 35 percent increase in non-life profits, attributing this to the bad result in the first quarter of 1996 when a severe winter produced a loss in the United States.

Bart van der Feen of IRIS said ING's banking results would have enjoyed a full quarter's consolidation of the results of Poland's Bank Slaski and an increased stake in banking systems group Mendes Gans.
But he expected a "somewhat flat" financial transactions result due to a fall in the value of Brady bonds issued by Latin American countries, in which ING is an active player.

Dennis Ederzeel of Delta Lloyd Bank said stable interest rates and a good share market would have assisted ING in the first quarter. "Everything was in favour of the banks and insurance companies," he said.
Fox Pitt Kelton analyst Lewis Phillips saw the main boost to banking profits coming from commission and trading income with net interest income being fairly stable.
"Trends seem to be pretty favourable everywhere," said Phillips, whose 850 million guilder profit forecast was at the bottom end of expectations.

Analysts also expect a lower provision for bad debts than in the first quarter of 1996, while the transfer to the new fund for unexpected loan losses would be down on the transfer to the former former hidden reserves fund.
